description: One stretch of time a worker was actually on a task. A job interrupted twice is three segments, and the hour charged to it is their sum — NOT the wall clock from the first start to the last finish, which on a valve repair that interrupted an irrigation set would bill the irrigating to the repair. The segments are the record; `Farm Task Assignment.actual_duration_minutes` is their total.

fields.description: When this stretch of work began — a start, or a resume after a pause.
fields.label: Started

fields.description: When it stopped. EMPTY MEANS THIS SEGMENT IS STILL RUNNING, which is the one open segment an in-progress assignment carries; a paused or completed assignment has none.
fields.label: Ended

fields.description: Minutes in this segment, computed when it closes. Stored rather than derived so a total does not change when somebody corrects a clock, and so a report can sum a column.
fields.label: Minutes

fields.description: What closed this segment. `auto_pause` is the one worth telling apart: the worker did not pause this job, they started another one and the server paused this for them — which is a different sentence in front of a payroll question about the gap.
fields.label: Ended By

fields.description: Why the worker stopped. 'Called to the valve at Home-7' is what makes a fragmented afternoon legible six weeks later.
fields.label: Reason

name: Task Time Segment
